LLM_description:
Situation:
Severe storm damage has disrupted ground lines of communication across the Riverine District. Supply Depot Alpha (inland) and Supply Depot Bravo (coastal) are operational with limited on-hand stocks of critical commodities. Supported sites requiring immediate resupply are Field Hospital Echo, Urban Shelter Complex Lima, IDP Camp Sierra, and Mountain Village Cluster Kilo. Primary corridors include a valley route exposed to sporadic insecurity and an alternate coastal corridor with intermittent landslide blockages. Airlift is unavailable this period; all movements will be by road with convoy discipline and security coordination.

Mission:
Relief Task Force Foxtrot conducts same-period ground distribution from Supply Depot Alpha and Supply Depot Bravo to the four supported sites to meet life-sustaining needs while minimizing total operational cost (variable transport, shortage penalties, vehicle deployment, and fixed route security risk costs).

Execution/Concept:
- Priorities: Water, medical materiel, and other life-sustaining items to Field Hospital Echo and IDP Camp Sierra first, while maintaining minimum thresholds at Urban Shelter Complex Lima and Mountain Village Cluster Kilo. Cross-level stocks between depots as required.
- Depot constraints: Dispatches from each depot by commodity cannot exceed available stocks this period.
- Demand constraints: Each site’s requirement by commodity must be met by deliveries; shortfalls are allowed only as last resort and incur penalty costs representing humanitarian impact.
- Vehicle constraints: Standardized fleet with fixed capacity per vehicle. Commodity flows convert to volume; total volume per origin-destination lane determines required vehicle count. Each vehicle deployed incurs a cost.
- Route activation and risk: Vehicles may only travel on routes declared “active” for the period. Activating any route (sending one or more vehicles) triggers a fixed risk cost to cover escorts and route clearance, regardless of the number of vehicles dispatched on that route. This cost is incurred per active route per period.
- Fleet limit: Total vehicles dispatched across all depots and destinations cannot exceed available fleet. Concentrate loads to minimize the number of active routes unless risk or access dictates otherwise.
- Cost structure: Variable transport costs depend on origin-destination and commodity; shortage penalties apply to unmet demand; vehicle deployment costs accrue per vehicle; fixed risk costs accrue per activated route.
- Coordination: Movement Control Center synchronizes dispatch times with Security Liaison for escorts and clearance. Receiving sites confirm offload capacity and establish safe offload windows. Contingency plans in place for rapid reroute if a corridor closes.
